clue.text: Upper-class daughter about to join game that may lead to a mate and a title

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the two letters for upper-class and daughter are read backwards

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

parts.words: game that may lead to a mate
parts.note: chess is the board game that ends in checkmate

explanation.surface: A posh young woman is about to take up a game that might bring her a husband and a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns UD into DU; 'to join' simply attaches the game. 'Mate' looks like a spouse but means checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess holds a noble rank, the wife of a duke or a peeress in her own right, so the word is itself a title.

clue.text: What's stored by computers? It's a bit upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue means turned upside down, so the phrase is read bottom to top

parts.note: a tad is a bit, a small amount

explanation.surface: Something computers store is mildly upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns A TAD upside down. 'a bit' is also a computing word, which is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Data is the information held in computer storage.

clue.text: Policeman has hour in type of aircraft

indicators.note: in says the hour letter goes inside the word for policeman

parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: A police officer spends an hour in a type of aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts H inside COPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopper is the informal word for a helicopter, a kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Anxious time limited by hesitation

indicators.note: limited by means held in on both sides, so the hesitation goes round the time

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A nervous person keeps hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited by' means hemmed in on both sides; 'Anxious' here is in the sense of keen, anxious to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen or impatiently wanting, close to the sense of anxious to do something.

clue.text: Like some stamps — but not for letter in Kent!

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, SE
the one who lets a property is the landlord; the tenant is the other party

explanation.surface: A stamp collector notes that some stamps are not for sending letters in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is someone who lets out property, not a piece of mail; a tenant rents rather than lets. Kent is a county in the south-east (SE) of England. Se-tenant stamps are printed joined in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Se-tenant is the philatelic term for stamps of different designs printed side by side.

clue.text: Noticed expression of resignation — I left drawn

parts.note: a sigh is the sound of someone resigned to their fate

indicators.note: left means gone away, so the letter I departs from the word for drawn

parts.note: a drawn game is a tied one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gave a resigned sigh and walked away from a match that ended level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' here is a game ending level (TIED); 'left' takes its I out to leave TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighted, in the sense of spotted or caught sight of, is a synonym of noticed.

clue.text: Poet needs minimal society and a very quiet house

indicators.note: minimal means reduced to the least, just the first letter of the word

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A poet wants a small social circle and a silent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minimal' keeps only the S of society; PP is pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was an ancient Greek lyric poet from Lesbos.

clue.text: Allowed member of family to have piece of furniture

parts.note: gran, a grandmother, is a member of the family
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A relative is permitted to have a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grantable may be granted, that is, it can be allowed.

clue.text: State of semiconsciousness requires injection of heroin' batch supplied

indicators.note: requires injection of means a letter is put inside the state

parts.note: a trance is a half-conscious state
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user drifts off after injecting heroin from a delivered batch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires injection of' puts H inside TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or instalment, especially of money or shares, so a batch.

clue.text: Protest left one building destroyed

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
I is the Roman numeral for one
a shed is a small building

explanation.surface: Protesters left after one building was wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolished means knocked down or wrecked, a synonym of destroyed.

clue.text: Like something that's been invented but placed the wrong way round

parts.note: though can stand for but, as in 'small though strong'

indicators.note: the wrong way round says the word for placed is read backwards

parts.note: to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: An invention seems to have been assembled back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' reverses the word for placed, giving TUP; 'but' is the synonym that starts the answer, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thought up has been devised or invented in someone's head.

clue.text: Panic as a hit secures run

indicators.note: secures means holds safely inside, so the run letter sits within the other pieces

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A batsman panics as a big hit brings in a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' puts R inside A + LAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is a sudden fear or panic, as in 'cause alarm'.

clue.text: Pan the article that's bad (as this writing is)

indicators.note: bad suggests the words are spoiled and put in a new order

parts.note: the three words are used as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A critic slates an article for being badly written, adding an aside in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges all the letters of PAN THE ARTICLE. The definition points to the brackets round '(as this writing is)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Words placed in brackets, as an aside, are parenthetical remarks.

clue.text: Suitability for the moment conveyed by words of drama in our paper

indicators.note: in says the drama words sit inside the newspaper name

parts.note: the clue appears in the Times newspaper
an actor's lines are the words of a play

explanation.surface: A writer's well-timed dramatic dialogue appears in this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our paper' is the Times, the paper printing the puzzle; 'in' puts LINES inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Timeliness is being well-timed or opportune, suited to the moment.

clue.text: I shout angrily without slowing down, creating nuisance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shout goes round the musical term

parts.note: to rant is to shout angrily
rit, short for ritardando, is the musical direction for slowing down

explanation.surface: Someone yells furiously without letting up, making themselves a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'slowing down' is the musical direction ritardando, abbreviated in scores.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is anything or anyone that annoys, a synonym for a nuisance.

clue.text: Having cut short attire, men look silly

indicators.note: look silly suggests the letters are put into a foolish new order

explanation.surface: Men whose clothes have been cropped look ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look silly' rearranges ATTIRE MEN. 'Cut short' looks like it describes the clothes but defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to end it, so to cut it short.

clue.text: Prey on wicked bosses

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: Cruel managers take advantage of their staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges BOSSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to prey on someone's mind continually, troubling them.

clue.text: Expert wined and dined, one of three females emerging as hit

indicators.note: emerging means leaving, so one of the three F letters for females drops out

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
to be feted is to be entertained lavishly

explanation.surface: An expert who has been entertained is suddenly struck.
explanation.walkthrough: BUFF + FETED has three Fs (F is short for female); 'one of three females emerging' removes one.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffeted means struck repeatedly, battered, so hit.

clue.text: Item sent abroad no longer left

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A parcel sent overseas has gone and is no longer there.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT is the nautical word for the left-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: An export is a product sent to another country for sale.

clue.text: Energy rising and falling? Biochemical compound needed

parts.note: pep is energy or vigour
the tide rises and falls twice a day

explanation.surface: A scientist asks whether a fluctuating energy level calls for some biochemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' tempts a reversal, but PEP reads the same either way; 'rising and falling' is the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: A peptide is a chain of amino acids, a compound studied in biochemistry.

clue.text: Employ cover cased in iron for part of plane

indicators.note: cased in means enclosed, so the two pieces sit within the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
to employ is to use
to lag pipes is to cover them with insulation

explanation.surface: A workman insulates something in an iron casing for an aircraft part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cased in' means enclosed by; 'cover' is the verb for insulating pipes or a boiler, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main body of an aircraft, one of its parts.

clue.text: Can aid first bit of tummy upset?

definitions.text: Can aid first bit of tummy upset?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are scrambled
first bit of keeps only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something can help the early stages of an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first bit of' gives T; 'upset' rearranges CAN AID + T. The whole clue also describes the remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid neutralises stomach acid and so can soothe a tummy upset.

clue.text: Like to stay next in city

indicators.note: in says the word for next sits inside the word for like

parts.note: as can mean like, as in 'as a child'
then means next in sequence

explanation.surface: Someone would like to stay on in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'to stay' is surface padding that pictures the word for next staying inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: Actually throw into panic when superior sort of bloke comes in

indicators.note: comes in says the upper-class fellow enters the scrambled letters
throw means mix up, so these words are scrambled

parts.note: a toff is a posh, upper-class man

explanation.surface: A posh man arrives and throws everyone into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase about panic reads as one idiom, but 'throw' is the anagram signal, giving INPOINACT, and 'comes in' places the posh fellow inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'in point of fact' is an idiom meaning really or as a matter of fact.

clue.text: Silver set before primate for ecclesiastical feast

indicators.note: set before means the silver symbol comes in front of the primate

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Silverware is laid out before a bishop at a church banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' suggests an archbishop, but here it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: An agape was a love feast shared by early Christians, a church meal.

clue.text: Person looking after cathedral gives priority to ace port

indicators.note: gives priority to means the named letter is moved to the front

parts.note: a dean is head of a cathedral chapter
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A cathedral official puts a top person first at the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives priority to' moves the A of DEAN to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen on the Gulf of Aden.

clue.text: Shrub takes a long time to absorb most of water, when very cold

indicators.note: to absorb means to take inside, so the era goes round the other piece

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word for frozen water

parts.note: water when frozen is ice

explanation.surface: A plant takes ages to soak up icy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter, leaving IC; 'to absorb' means taking it inside. Erica is the heath or heather genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths, low evergreen shrubs.

clue.text: Delighted to find a fourth way in?

parts.note: an entrance is a way in
D is the fourth letter, as in entrances labelled A, B, C, D

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to find yet another door into a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Large buildings label doors A, B, C...; a fourth one would be ENTRANCE D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be entranced is to be enchanted or filled with delight.

clue.text: Types of plants turning a particular colour, with spots on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the word for spots surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to spot is to see, so spots means sees

indicators.note: turning means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a particular colour

explanation.surface: Some plants change colour and develop spotted edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the colour to DER; 'on the outside' means the word for spots wraps round it, not that the plant has spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeders are plants classed by the way they reproduce, spreading by seed.

clue.text: China endorsed changes —- nothing to lose

indicators.note: changes means the letters are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Chinese policy was approved, then altered with nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O away from ENDORSED ('to lose') and rearrange ('changes') the rest. 'China' is porcelain, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is a fine porcelain made near the German city, so it is a kind of china.
